newsitem.title: USA: Conn. colleges urge more student financial aid.
newsitem.headline: Conn. colleges urge more student financial aid.

text.p: A group of independent Connecticut colleges and universities Wednesday urged state lawmakers to heed a survey showing that voters want more money for colleges.

The Quinnipiac College Poll released earlier on Wednesday found that Connecticut voters overwhelmingly favor plans to beef up support for state universities and to help parents and students pay for college education.
The survey "sends a clear message to Connecticut lawmakers that current student aid programs are under-funded," according to the Connecticut Conference of Independent Colleges (CCIC).
There is wide support for changing the tax system to help make college more affordable, CCIC President Michael Gerber said in a statement.

"It's time we started investing in our future by providing students from low- and middle-income families with greater access to educations at our independent and public colleges and universities," he said.
Gerber said Connecticut has never funded its own student financial aid programs at levels mandated by statute.
Funding financial aid programs at the levels set by law would require the state to allocate an additional $5 million to the Connecticut Independent College Student (CICS) grant program, he said.
It would also require an extra $16 million to the Connecticut Aid to Public College Students (CAPCS) grant program.
The state budget proposed by Republican Governor John Rowland would maintain funding for student aid at the same level it has been since the beginning of the decade.
The CICS program has been funded at $12.06 million every year since 1992, following cuts in 1990 and 1991.
The CAPCS program has been funded at $5.6 million every year since 1990.
Gerber said that funding those programs at the same levels year after year actually results in a decrease in the level of support to students who receive financial aid, due to inflation.
The CCIC represents 17 non-profit, independent colleges and universities in the state.
